Abstract.AbstractText: Auto-focused Virtual Source Imaging (AVSI) has been recently presented as an alternative method for Synthetic Aperture Focusing (SAFT) through arbitrarily shaped interfaces with arrays. This work extends the AVSI concept to the case of Total Focusing Method (TFM-AVSI) using several virtual receivers for each virtual source. This approach overcomes the known contrast limitation of AVSI, while preserving the advantage of performing synthetic focusing in the second medium only (no time-of-flight calculations through the interface). By counterpart, an equipment with more active channels must be used to digitalize the signals received by all the array elements after each focused emission. When compared with conventional TFM, the proposed method reduces the processing complexity of the most time consuming task: Time-of-flight calculation in the presence of interfaces. This improvement could lead to more efficient real-time implementations of TFM in Non-Destructive-Testing applications where water immersion or flexible wedges are used. In this work, the mathematical formulation for the new method is given, accounting for the surface slope and the array angular sensitivity. Its performance is evaluated by numerical simulation, experimentally and compared with AVSI and conventional TFM. It was found that TFM-AVSI achieves the same resolution and contrast than TFM, although shows a wider blind zone below the interface due to focusing with normal incidence.

Article.ArticleTitle: Total Focusing Method with Virtual Sources in the presence of unknown geometry interfaces.
